title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, Internal Tools (Comprehensive Guide)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This comprehensive handbook page provides the core information all Redwood employees need to get productive and plan their careers at the company. It covers role families and career ladders, benefits and perks highlights, the end-to-end hiring and onboarding workflow, and the primary internal tools and access patterns. People Ops maintains this page in partnership with Engineering, Product, and Recruiting.

1) Working at Redwood  Summary

- Mission: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.
- Culture pillars: engineering excellence, customer-first thinking, operational rigor, and continuous learning.
- Remote-first with hub offices in SF and London; we use flexible location bands in compensation and benefits.

2) Roles & Career Ladders

Redwood uses leveled role families with transparent expectations for impact, scope, and leadership. Role-level documents (linked from this page) provide competency matrices, sample deliverables, and promotion rubrics. High-level families:

- Engineering (IC and Manager tracks)
  - IC: Software Engineer I/II/Senior/Staff/Principal focus areas include runtime performance, infra, platform, and product features.
  - Manager: Eng Manager, Senior Eng Manager, Director of Engineering ownership of team delivery, hiring, and growth.
- Product & Design: Product Manager I/II/Senior/Lead; Product Designer I/II/Senior/Lead.
- Applied ML & Research: Applied Researcher I/II/Senior/Lead model evaluation, onboarding, and quantization research.
- SRE & Operations: SRE I/II/Senior/Lead SLO ownership, runbook authorship, incident response.
- GTM & Support: Sales, Solutions, Customer Success tiers aligned to quota and strategic account ownership.
- People Ops, Finance, Legal: IC ladders and manager ladders for operations functions.

Promotion process (high level):
1. Manager and employee prepare a calibration packet with impact examples and metrics.
2. Peer and cross-functional reviewers provide feedback.
3. Calibration committee evaluates against ladder rubrics and produces a recommendation.
4. HR communicates outcomes and updates HRIS.

3) Benefits & Perks (high-level summary)

Full plan details live in the Benefits Portal. Highlights:

- Compensation: market-competitive base salary, RSU grants at hire and on a refresh cadence, and a discretionary bonus program for eligible roles.
- Health: employer-subsidized medical, dental, and vision plans in the US; region-equivalent plans for international employees.
- Time off: baseline 20 days PTO (US full-time) plus company holidays; additional PTO provisions per local law and tenure.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver up to 18 weeks paid; secondary caregiver up to 12 weeks paid; flexible caregiver leave available.
- Learning & development: $2,000 annual learning stipend, team training budget, and approved conference attendance.
- Remote & office: one-time home office stipend and recurring allowance; commuter subsidy for hub-office employees.
- Wellness: EAP, mental health benefits, and monthly wellness stipend.

Key benefits at-a-glance (quick reference):
- PTO: 20 days + company holidays (increases with tenure and per local law)
- Parental leave: Primary 18 weeks; Secondary 12 weeks
- Health: Employer-subsidized medical/dental/vision or local equivalent
- Learning stipend: $2,000/year
- Equity: RSU grants at hire and standard refresh cadence

4) Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Recruiting process (candidate experience):
1. Application and resume screen by Recruiting.
2. Hiring manager phone screen (30-45 minutes).
3. Role-specific interviews (typically 3-5 loops for engineering).
4. Culture / bar-raiser interview.
5. Take-home or live exercise when applicable.
6. Hiring committee review and offer approval.
7. Offer extended and background check completed where required.

Time-to-offer targets:
- Individual contributor engineering roles: 3-5 weeks.
- Sales and customer-facing roles: 4-6 weeks.

New hire checklist (Day 0 Day 90):
- Day 0: HR forms completed, 1Password access created, Okta SSO provisioned, equipment shipped/tracked.
- Day 1: Orientation (People Ops), manager welcome, team introductions, handbook and security walkthrough.
- Week 1: GitHub and cloud project access requested, first-week goals and learning plan established.
- 30 days: complete security training, close first onboarding ticket or small project, meet cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: own an end-to-end task and present a demo or writeup to the team.
- 90 days: formal performance check-in and calibration discussion for leveling.

Manager onboarding responsibilities (priority checklist):
1. Share a documented 30/60/90 plan and assign the first PR/issue.
2. Schedule weekly 1:1s for the first 3 months.
3. Ensure access to required services and invite to recurring meetings.
4. Assign a peer buddy and a project mentor.

5) Internal Tools & Access Guide

Primary tools and how to get access:
- Okta (SSO) People Ops: core SSO provider; new employees provisioned automatically.
- 1Password People Ops: company vault for secrets and shared credentials.
- Google Workspace IT: email, Drive, and Calendar.
- Slack Eng & DX: primary communications. Join #all, #announcements, and team channels.
- GitHub Engineering: repo access is managed with GitHub Teams; request access via the Access Request Confluence form.
- Jira Product/Eng: project-level access controlled by project admins.
- Confluence Documentation: team pages and handbook; edit rights for team spaces.
- PagerDuty SRE: on-call management and incident notifications.
- Datadog / Grafana Observability: read access by default; write access needs Eng Platform approval.
- Redwood CLI & Dev Cluster Eng Infra: request dev cluster access following the dev-cluster onboarding doc.

Access request process (step-by-step):
1. Core services are provisioned automatically via HRIS -> Okta flow.
2. For role-specific services (repos, cloud projects, monitoring), open an Access Request ticket in Jira and tag your manager.
3. Manager and service owner approvals are required; automated provisioning completes where available.
4. Target SLA for role-specific access provisioning: 48 business hours.
5. Escalation: if SLA is missed, CC People Ops and Eng Platform with the Jira ticket.

Security & best practices:
- Store secrets only in 1Password; do not commit secrets to repos.
- Enforce MFA on all accounts (Okta policy).
- Follow the Secure SDLC guidance and code review checklists in security-and-compliance.

6) Learning, Mentorship & Career Development

- Mentorship program: quarterly opt-in; People Ops manages pairing and matching.
- Career conversations: recommended at least annually with manager and during promotion cycles.
- Internal training: rotating Lunch & Learns, quarterly engineering guilds, and role-specific workshops.
- Conference support: manager-approved attendance with People Ops and Finance coordination for larger events.

7) Frequently Asked Questions (selected)

Q: How do I change my compensation location band or request relocation?
A: Submit a Location Change form to People Ops; approvals consider role, compensation, and business needs.

Q: How are external conference requests handled?
A: Manager approval is required; People Ops and Finance handle travel booking and reimbursement when applicable.

8) Ownership & Contacts

- People Ops (primary owner): handbook content, benefits administration, onboarding (people-ops@redwood.com).
- Eng Platform: access provisioning, dev clusters, observability (eng-platform@redwood.com).
- Security: secure-sdlc guidance, training, and incident response (security@redwood.com).

Change control: People Ops maintains this page. Major changes (benefits, parental leave, leveling) require review by Finance and Legal. Minor edits may be made directly with a short note in the page history.

Related pages: role-specific ladders, onboarding runbooks, benefits portal, security onboarding checklist.
